passage: Hrithik's train ticket to the new city was booked for a fortnight away, so he and his father made a list on the fridge door: admission papers, bank card, medicines, clothes, phone numbers. Each evening one more line got a tick, and the bag itself was packed the night before. Meanwhile Tejas and his parents sat with a laptop, comparing a hostel and two paying-guest rooms. He read reviews, called a senior about the walk to college, food and safety, and the family travelled there to look around before handing over any deposit. Pankaj arrived in the same city certain he would feel at home by Friday. By the third week the corridor was quiet, his phone stayed silent, and he told his mother, "I want to come back. I can't do this." Hrithik, too, ran into trouble: he skipped breakfast most mornings and read the same page three times. So he set fixed hours for meals, found a tiffin service on the next lane, and moved his study time to late evening when the hostel went quiet.

qa.q: What did Hrithik and his father put on the fridge door?
qa.a: They put up a list of things to take, including admission papers, bank card, medicines, clothes and phone numbers, and ticked one more line each evening.

qa.q: How did Tejas's preparation differ from Pankaj's expectations about the new city?
qa.a: Tejas and his parents researched, asked a senior, and visited before paying. Pankaj simply assumed he would fit in by Friday, so the lonely third week hit him hard.

qa.q: What was Pankaj feeling when he told his mother he wanted to come back?
qa.a: Pankaj felt lonely and panicked, because his expectation of quickly feeling at home had not come true.

qa.q: What could Pankaj try before deciding to leave?
qa.a: He could talk to his mother about the loneliness, then take small steps such as joining a group or greeting one neighbour each day, and give himself time to settle. If the low mood stays, he could speak to a counsellor at the college. 🤍

grounding: Students moving to a new city plan with a checklist, research housing, expect instant belonging and struggle, or adjust routines after early problems.
